label: Network tuning *More parallel connections per server (10 instead of 6), request pacing off (Firefox inserts small deliberate delays between request bursts; on a fast line they are pure latency), more speculative connections, and larger DNS and TLS-session caches so repeat visits skip lookups and handshakes. Every value is snapshotted before it is changed; turning this off restores your profile exactly, and any pref you later change by hand is left alone as yours.*

Predictor on https hover *Firefox's network predictor learns which connections a page will need. This extends it to act on link hover over https and to prefetch what it is confident about, so the click lands on work already done.*

Less session-store disk churn *Session state is written to disk every 15 seconds by default, a periodic jank source on hard drives and busy systems. This halves the cadence to every 30 seconds. The trade: after a hard crash, up to 30 seconds of very recent tab changes are lost instead of 15. Zen's window sync is unaffected.*

Bigger in-memory media cache *64 MB of RAM for streamed media, so small seeks in video replay from memory instead of re-fetching from the network. Memory-for-network trade; turn off on low-RAM machines.*

Smooth workspace switching *Suspends tab blur effects and transitions ONLY for the duration of the workspace slide animation, using the marker attribute Zen itself sets while it runs. Blurred tab backgrounds re-render their blur every frame while the strip moves, which is what makes switching feel framey with glass themes; parked, they cost little and come straight back the instant the slide ends. Resting visuals are pixel-identical.*

Force GPU rendering paths *Enables WebRender and accelerated canvas on hardware where Mozilla's blocklist keeps them off conservatively. Changes nothing on machines where they already run -- ZenTurbo.status() shows whether this pack is managing any prefs. If you see visual glitches, turn it off; your profile is restored exactly.*

Warm connections on hover *Hovering an unloaded tab or a bookmark pre-opens the TCP and TLS connection to its site, in the right container, so DNS, handshake and certificate work happen during the hover instead of after the click. Pairs with Tab Unloader: unloaded tabs reload onto an already-open socket. Throttled to once per site per minute; loaded tabs cost nothing.*

Warm connections on link hover *Extends hover warmup into web pages: hovering a link opens the TCP and TLS connection to wherever it points, so a click lands on a socket that already exists. A chrome script cannot see mouse events inside a page, so this hooks the function Firefox already calls to show a link's target in the corner status panel -- it fires on every link hover there is. The connection is opened in the container of the tab you are hovering in, since that is where the link would open. Same throttle as the rest: an origin is not re-warmed while its socket is still alive.*

Warm frequent sites at startup *The first visit of a session pays DNS and TLS cold. Shortly after startup this reads your most-visited sites from history (read-only, local) and pre-opens connections to them, spread out a quarter second apart. Your first real navigation of the day lands warm.*
How many sites to warm at startup *Top sites by visit frequency. Each warm connection is one open socket; more than a dozen is rarely useful.*
Startup warmup delay (milliseconds) *How long after the window is ready before warming begins, so it never competes with session restore for the network.*

Measure whether warming actually helps *Counts every connection this mod opens ahead of time, then checks each navigation against it: did a real request land on that socket before the browser closed it? `ZenTurbo.stats()` reports the hit rate and the worst offenders by origin. A warmed socket only survives `network.http.keep-alive.timeout` -- 115 seconds by default -- and anything later is counted as a miss, so the number is not flattered. This exists because "it feels faster" is exactly the claim this mod refuses to make: if the rate is low, the warming is aimed wrong and should be turned off. Costs one lookup per page load.*

Log what it is doing *Prints to the Browser Console (Ctrl+Shift+J) under [ZenTurbo]. ZenTurbo.status() lists active packs and every pref currently managed; ZenTurbo.log() shows recent activity including each warmed connection.*
